content.text:
phpstan-guard-rulesにおいてrectorサポートを入れてください。
つまりルール単位に安全な変更、リスクある変更、自動変更不可で選別し、安全、リスクある変更をrectorでできるようにルール提供してください。またどのルールは変更可能かなどはdocsの各種ルールや一覧に記載ください。
既存ルールを確認し、安全な修正・リスクのある修正・自動修正不可に分類します。Rectorルールとテストを追加し、各ルールの説明と一覧にも対応状況を記載します。RectorのAPI確認にはfind-docsスキルを使います。

*** Add File: /Users/ab/Projects/php-ai-toolkit/packages/phpstan-guard-rules/docs/rector.md
+# Rector Support
+
+The package provides ten optional Rector rules: two safe transformations and
+eight transformations that require review. Every PHPStan rule is classified in
+the [rule list](phpstan-rules.md); each rule page explains its supported cases,
+risks, or reason automatic changes are unavailable.
+
+## Installation
+
+Install Rector in the consuming project:
+
+```sh
+composer require --dev rector/rector:^2.6.7
+```
+
+The supported Rector runtime is `^2.6.7` with PHP 8.0 or later. Rector 2 requires
+PHPStan 2. The PHPStan extension itself still supports `^1.12 || ^2.0`, and
+installing this package does not require Rector. Projects retaining PHPStan 1
+must run Rector from a separate tool installation with this package installed.
+
+## Safe Changes
+
+Create `rector.php` in your project:
+
+```php
+<?php
+
+use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
+
+return RectorConfig::configure()
+    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
+    ->withSets([
+        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
+    ]);
+```
+
+Preview the changes, then apply them:
+
+```sh
+vendor/bin/rector process --dry-run
+vendor/bin/rector process
+```
+
+The safe set preserves executable behavior and documented contract contents in
+the supported cases. It expands single-line public PHPDoc and adds `#[Override]`
+where the existing PHPStan rule confirms a valid concrete parent override.
+The new attribute is observable through reflection; projects that instantiate
+attributes on PHP before 8.3 need an `Override` polyfill or can select only the
+PHPDoc rule. Line-number-sensitive code or tools may observe formatting changes.
+
+## Risky Changes
+
+Risky rules can change runtime behavior, declared types or exceptions, test
+documentation, or analysis suppressions. Their implementation is deliberately
+limited to specific patterns, and they leave unsupported cases unchanged.
+Review the diff and run PHPStan and the test suite after applying them.
+
+Add the risky set explicitly alongside the safe set when those changes are
+appropriate for your project:
+
+```php
+return RectorConfig::configure()
+    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src', __DIR__ . '/tests'])
+    ->withSets([
+        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/safe.php',
+        __DIR__ . '/vendor/k-kinzal/phpstan-guard-rules/rector/risky.php',
+    ]);
+```
+
+The risky set does not import the safe set, and the safe set never imports risky
+rules. Neither set registers itself automatically through `rules.neon`.
+
+| PHPStan rule | Rector class in `Toolkit\Rector` | Category |
+|-------------|----------------------------------|----------|
+| [ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule](rules/ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRule.md#rector) | `ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector` | Safe |
+| [OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule](rules/OverrideMustHaveAttributeRule.md#rector) | `OverrideMustHaveAttributeRector` | Safe |
+| [ForbiddenCommentRule](rules/ForbiddenCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenCommentRector` | Risky |
+| [ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule](rules/ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRule.md#rector) | `ForbiddenMagicMethodCallRector` | Risky |
+| [ForbidNonDocCommentRule](rules/ForbidNonDocCommentRule.md#rector) | `ForbidNonDocCommentRector` | Risky |
+| [ForbidEmptyCatchRule](rules/ForbidEmptyCatchRule.md#rector) | `ForbidEmptyCatchRector` | Risky |
+| [RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule](rules/RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRule.md#rector) | `RequireThrowsTagOnDirectThrowRector` | Risky |
+| [RequireExceptionChainingRule](rules/RequireExceptionChainingRule.md#rector) | `RequireExceptionChainingRector` | Risky |
+| [RequireListForArrayLiteralRule](rules/RequireListForArrayLiteralRule.md#rector) | `RequireListForArrayLiteralRector` | Risky |
+| [ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule](rules/ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRule.md#rector) | `ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector` | Risky |
+
+## Selecting Individual Rules
+
+Use `withRules()` to select individual transformations:
+
+```php
+use Rector\Config\RectorConfig;
+use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector;
+use Toolkit\Rector\RequireExceptionChainingRector;
+
+return RectorConfig::configure()
+    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/src'])
+    ->withRules([
+        ForbidSingleLinePhpDocRector::class,
+        RequireExceptionChainingRector::class,
+    ]);
+```
+
+Rector does not read `parameters.toolkit` from `phpstan.neon`. Keep the selected
+rules, paths, skips, and test namespace prefixes aligned with your PHPStan policy.
+For custom restricted test namespaces, configure the prose-removal rule:
+
+```php
+use Toolkit\Rector\ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector;
+
+return RectorConfig::configure()
+    ->withPaths([__DIR__ . '/tests'])
+    ->withConfiguredRule(ForbidDescriptivePhpDocInTestClassRector::class, [
+        'Project\Tests\Unit',
+        'Project\Tests\Integration',
+    ]);
+```
+
+## Unavailable Changes
+
+Rules classified as unavailable require decisions about domain types, public
+APIs, dependency ownership, test scenarios, or meaningful assertions. The package
+does not invent examples, remove assertions, widen visibility, or add arbitrary
+dispatch branches to make those diagnostics disappear. Follow the manual repair
+instructions on the corresponding rule page.
+
+## Verification
+
+The unit suite runs the real Rector CLI against before/after fixtures for every
+provided transformation. It checks unchanged unsupported cases and runs Rector
+again in dry-run mode to detect non-idempotent changes. Run it from the package:
+
+```sh
+composer test:unit -- --filter Rector
+```
+
+See the upstream [custom rule documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/custom-rule)
+and [set documentation](https://getrector.com/documentation/sets) for Rector configuration concepts.
